facts.statement: Thaumatosaurus is an extinct genus of plesiosaur whose name means 'wonder reptile'.
facts.quote: Thaumatosaurus (Meaning 'wonder reptile') is a dubious extinct genus of plesiosaur.

facts.statement: The genus Thaumatosaurus was described by paleontologist Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer in 1841.
facts.quote: The name Thaumatosaurus, which means 'wonder reptile', belonged to a genus of plesiosaur that was described by palaeontologist Christian Erich Hermann von Meyer, back in 1841.

facts.statement: Thaumatosaurus is currently considered a nomen dubium because its holotype can only be identified as an indeterminate plesiosaur.
facts.quote: Today this taxon is regarded as a nomen dubium because the holotype can be referred to Pliosauroidea indet at best.

facts.statement: Specimens once attributed to Thaumatosaurus are now recognized as the holotypes for the genera Eurycleidus, Meyerasaurus, and Rhomaleosaurus.
facts.quote: The diagnostic specimens which previously were regarded as Thaumatosauruss specimens, now represent the holotypes of Eurycleidus, Meyerasaurus and Rhomaleosaurus.

facts.statement: Thaumatosaurus belongs to the family Plesiosauridae.
Thaumatosaurus lived during the Bathonian stage, between 168.2 and 165.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Bathonian (168.2 to 165.3 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The species Thaumatosaurus oolithicus was described based on partial skull, vertebral, and limb remains found in the Posidonia Shale of Holzmaden, Germany.
rejected.quote: Meyer described the species Thaumatosaurus oolithicus based on partial skull, vertebral and limb remains, that were found in the Posidonia Shale of Holzmaden, Baden-Württemberg, Germany.
